editorial:
If you love a good mind-bending thriller, Who Am I is a hidden gem you should not miss. The story follows Benjamin, a shy young German computer whiz who feels invisible in everyday life. When he gets pulled into a rebellious hacker group that wants to make a name for itself on the world stage, things quickly spiral out of control. The movie has a slick, stylish energy that keeps you guessing, and the hacker culture backdrop feels fresh and exciting rather than cheesy. It is the kind of film that grabs you early and refuses to let go.

The acting is strong across the board, especially the lead performance, which carries the emotional weight of the story. The pacing is tight, the twists land well, and the action scenes are sharp without feeling over the top. On the downside, a few plot turns require you to suspend disbelief, and the tech jargon can feel a bit much at times. Still, if you enjoy clever thrillers with a dark edge, this one is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Benjamin confesses to the police and reveals that his hacker friends were not real people at all. They were all parts of his own mind, created by his dissociative identity disorder. He had been the mastermind behind every hack and crime the whole time. Just when it seems he will be locked away, the last twist shows he planned his own escape. The police van drives off with him smiling, proving he outsmarted everyone and walked away free.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever thrillers with big twists.
